text:
alex: FYI ran a longctx workload across an H100/MI250X pair and hit a weird KV cache page re-entry pattern. memory keeps growing on MI side. logs show page.age resetting on a remap path, leading to reuse counters undercounting and eviction not keeping up.

maya: can you paste a minimal repro + config?

alex: repro is pretty small: run local hybrid test with paged-attn model, seq=16k, batch=2, concurrent 8 sessions. command:```./tools/run_perf --model paged-llm --seq 16384 --batch 2 --concurrency 8 --gpus h100,mi250x --kv-policy paged``` logs attached: snippets below.

alex: log snippet (timestamps are ms from test start):
```
[12045] pager: allocate page id=0x7f8 owner=dev0 age=1
[12047] kv: remap page id=0x7f8 -> owner=dev1 (move)
[12048] pager: allocate page id=0x7f8 owner=dev1 age=0
[12050] kv: reuse hit on page id=0x7f8 age=0
[12060] pager: eviction skipped page id=0x7f8 age=0 reuse_count=1
[12345] mem_total_dev1 +12MB
[13000] mem_total_dev1 +24MB
```

raj: interesting — looks like remap path zeroes age when switch owner. could be race between remap and compaction/evict completion. on H100 we use fused-kernel eviction path, on MI we go through the async completion that calls back into pager on the CPU. ordering diff could explain it.

maya: does the pager use same lock ordering on both remap and eviction paths? iirc there was a known inversion: remap grabs page_lock then owner_lock, evict completion sometimes grabs owner_lock then page_lock.

dmitri: sounds plausible. i dug into pager.cc and there's a fast path where remap does: acquire(page->lock) ; if (page->owner != new_owner) page->owner = new_owner; page->age = 0; release(page->lock); while evict completion does: acquire(owner->lock); acquire(page->lock); clear mapping; release(page->lock); release(owner->lock); That inversion can cause a window where age gets set then overwritten or lost.

alex: i ran counters: eviction_attempts, eviction_success, reuse_hits, mapped_pages. numbers for MI250x over 30s window: eviction_attempts=1243, eviction_success=812, reuse_hits=203, mapped_pages=1876, mem_growth=~34MB. H100 same run: eviction_attempts=1285, eviction_success=1240, reuse_hits=920, mapped_pages=980, mem_growth=~2MB.

maya: big delta. reuse_hits so much lower on MI. that matches age being reset/zeroed so eviction logic thinks page is young.

dmitri: quick mitigation: CAS owner pointer in remap and make evict completion use a try-lock ordering, or introduce a short quiesce in remap when owner changes. simplest low-risk change: set page->age = max(page->age, 1) after remap, and add telemetry to detect owner flip events per-page.

raj: we should avoid band-aids. better to fix lock ordering. change evict completion to acquire page_lock first when possible. but careful: that could increase contention on hot pages. maybe do compare-and-swap on owner to ensure we don't race.

alex: quick test: added atomic CAS on page->owner in remap path (pseudo): ```old = atomic_load(&page->owner); if (old!=new) atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&page->owner, &old, new); page->age = (old==new)? page->age : 1;``` result: mem_growth drops to ~6MB and reuse_hits go up to 610. still occasional spikes.

ci-bot: build/runtime_tests (mi250x) #874 queued — longctx-hybrid failing on baseline (pre-change) with pager assertion: "evict_completion: page->owner == expected_owner" at pager.cc:412

alex: i also instrumented the order of locks in traces. short trace:
```
[34210] thread-A: remap start -> acquire page_lock
[34211] thread-B: evict cb -> acquire owner_lock
[34212] thread-A: remap sets owner -> release page_lock
[34213] thread-B: evict cb -> acquire page_lock (sees stale owner) -> clears mapping -> release page_lock
[34214] remap sees cleared mapping and resets age -> race observed
```

maya: that's the exact re-entry. we need to ensure evict cb always checks owner via CAS after acquiring page_lock, or refactor to single canonical lock.

dmitri: proposed code sketch in slack style:```// evict cb
acquire(owner_lock);
acquire(page_lock);
if (page->owner != owner) { release(page_lock); release(owner_lock); return; }
// proceed clear mapping
release(page_lock); release(owner_lock);
// remap path
acquire(page_lock);
old = atomic_load(&page->owner);
if (old != expected) atomic_compare_exchange(&page->owner, &old, new);
page->age = (old==new) ? page->age : 1;
release(page_lock);
```

alex: i'll run a 10m hybrid run with CAS + extra assert to detect double-remap and collect perf traces.

raj: if that passes, add a deterministic unit test that injects evict-cb scheduling after remap to reproduce in CI. also add perf regression alert for longctx mem growth.

alex: opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/874 — includes CAS fix + telemetry + longctx-hybrid perf test.

ci-bot: PR #874 build queued. current diff: +85 -12. longctx-hybrid perf check scheduled.

maya: thanks. once CI is green let's run on a farm of mixed nodes (h100/mi/rtx) to be safe. also add note to release notes about pager lock ordering fix and hybrid GPU stability. :thumbsup:

alex: will do. will paste perf summary once 10m run finishes. :hourglass:
